answer: Correlation clustering pays a cluster, not a key. Each epoch the ledger compares every pair of agents on submit timing, network origin and answer embeddings; pairs that match on all three for 3 epochs running are tied onto one trellis and split a single reward. An attacker whose keys rise on the same tide of requests from one server gets merged, so each extra key only earns if it runs its own model, host and schedule, which costs as much as an honest agent. A key reaches the summit of a full share only after 10 uncorrelated epochs.
